_comment: Grow's Wasitiyya world: al-Aqida al-Wasitiyya, Ibn Taymiyya's creed, section by section, lesson by lesson. Hand-written. Every `ar` and `source` is the book's own words, from backend/data/books/openiti/<file> (the Shamela edition, whose editor numbered the passages: those numbers and bracketed titles are headings the parts read through, `continues`); src/lib/bookLesson.test.js checks each. `en` and `why` are our English, written from the standard commentaries (Ibn ʿUthaymin, al-Harras), never quoted. We teach what Ibn Taymiyya says in plain words; where the Ashʿarī school reads a line differently, a neutral Note says so and nothing is asked on it.
_cards: teach {title, ar, en} · choose {ask, ar?, options, answer: index, source, why} — an `ar` with ____ is a gap the answer fills · pick {ask, options: [{text, right?}], source, why} · sort {ask, into, items: [[text, bucket]], source, why} · order {ask, steps (in the right order), source, why}. `source` may be one quote or a list.
author: Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyya (d. 728 AH)
madhhab: Atharī creed (Ahl al-Hadith; the Salafi school today)
continues: [12- ينشئ الله للجنة أقواما فيدخلهم إياها] :
[إثبات أن القرآن منزل من الله تعالى] :
[صفات المكر والكيد والمحال لله تعالى على ما يليق بجلاله] :

glossary.en: Tawqifi: fixed by the texts; Allah's names and attributes are taken from the Qur'an and Sunna, not reasoned out.
Tahrif: twisting a text's wording or meaning away from what it says.
Taʿṭīl: denying all or some of the attributes the texts give Allah.
Takyif: asking or claiming how an attribute is.
Tamthil: likening Allah's attributes to those of creation.
Ilhad in the names: turning them from their meaning, denying them, or giving them to others.
Nafy and ithbat: Allah describes Himself by denying what does not befit Him and affirming what does.
Attributes of the essence, such as life and knowledge, that Allah always has.
Attributes of act, such as love, pleasure and anger: tied to His will, eternal in their kind, each instance occurring when He wills.
Kawniyya will: what Allah decrees to happen; it always comes to pass, loved or not.
Shar'iyya will: what Allah loves and commands; His slaves may or may not do it.

parts.title: The pillars of faith, and how Allah is described
kitabs: الابتعاد عن التحريف والتعطيل والتكييف والتمثيل

lessons.title: The saved group and the six pillars

cards.title: The opening
cards.ar: الحمد لله الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق؛ ليظهره على الدين كله وكفى بالله شهيدا.
cards.en: Ibn Taymiyya opens with praise to Allah who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion, and Allah suffices as witness: the Qur'an's own words (48:28).

cards.title: The two testimonies
cards.ar: وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له؛ إقرارا به وتوحيدا.
cards.en: He testifies that there is no god but Allah, alone without partner, 'acknowledging Him and declaring His oneness', and that Muhammad is His slave and messenger.

cards.ask: What does the subtitle call Ahl al-Sunna wal-Jama'a?
options: The saved and aided group, until the Hour
The group of the jurists of Iraq and their students everywhere
The group that wrote the most books of creed in the early centuries
cards.source: اعتقاد الفرقة الناجية المنصورة إلى قيام الساعة أهل السنة والجماعة
cards.why: al-firqa al-najiya al-mansura ila qiyam al-sa'a: saved, aided, lasting until the Hour.

cards.title: Whose creed this is
cards.ar: اعتقاد الفرقة الناجية المنصورة إلى قيام الساعة أهل السنة والجماعة
cards.en: The book's subtitle. The author presents Ahl al-Sunna wal-Jamaʿa as the saved and aided group, the names taken from the hadith of the sects and of the group that stays on the truth until the Hour.

cards.title: The six pillars
cards.ar: الإيمان بالله، وملائكته، وكتبه، ورسله، والبعث بعد الموت، والإيمان بالقدر؛ خيره وشره.
cards.en: Their belief is faith in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the resurrection after death, and the decree, its good and its bad: the six pillars of the hadith of Jibril.

cards.ask: Pick the six pillars as the book lists them.

options.text: The decree, its good and its bad

cards.source: الإيمان بالله، وملائكته، وكتبه، ورسله، والبعث بعد الموت، والإيمان بالقدر؛ خيره وشره.
cards.why: Six: Allah, angels, books, messengers, resurrection, decree with its good and bad.

cards.ask: Put the pillars in the order the book names them.
cards.source: الإيمان بالله، وملائكته، وكتبه، ورسله، والبعث بعد الموت، والإيمان بالقدر؛ خيره وشره.
cards.why: The order of the hadith of Jibril, which the book follows word for word.

lessons.title: Describing Allah as He described Himself
lessons.arabic: الإيمان بما وصف الله به نفسه

cards.title: Two sources of description
cards.ar: ومن الإيمان بالله:
cards.en: Part of faith in Allah is to believe in what He described Himself with in His Book and what His Messenger ﷺ described Him with. The attributes are taken from these two (tawqīfī); reason does not set them, it follows what the texts give.

cards.ask: Where do Ahl al-Sunna take Allah's attributes from, in this book?
options: What Allah said of Himself in His Book and what His Messenger said of Him
What reason finds fitting for a perfect being, checked against the texts afterwards
What the philosophers established and the theologians refined over the centuries
source: - الإيمان بما وصف به نفسه في كتابه.
- وبما وصفه به رسوله محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.
cards.why: bima wasafa bihi nafsahu fi kitabihi, wa bima wasafahu bihi rasuluhu: the Book and the Sunna, nothing else.

cards.title: Without four things
cards.ar: من غير: تحريف ولا تعطيل، ومن غير: تكييف ولا تمثيل.
cards.en: They affirm those descriptions without tahrif (twisting the wording or meaning), ta'til (emptying Him of the attribute), takyif (asking how) or tamthil (likening to creation). Note: what the Ashʿarī school calls taʾwīl, argued from Arabic usage, this book counts as taḥrīf when it leaves the plain sense without a valid proof. Nothing is asked on which name is right.

cards.ask: Match each error to its name.
items: Reading 'His hand' as something other than what the words say
Denying that He has the attribute at all
Saying His hearing is like ours
cards.source: من غير: تحريف ولا تعطيل، ومن غير: تكييف ولا تمثيل.
cards.why: Tahrif changes the text, ta'til empties it, takyif asks how, tamthil likens.

cards.title: Nothing is like Him, and He hears and sees
cards.ar: بل يؤمنون بأن الله تعالى: {ليس كمثله شيء وهو السميع البصير}
cards.en: The verse that holds both sides together (42:11): 'There is nothing like Him' denies likeness, 'and He is the Hearing, the Seeing' affirms the attributes. Denial and affirmation in one breath.

cards.ar: بل يؤمنون بأن الله تعالى: {ليس كمثله شيء وهو ____}
cards.source: بل يؤمنون بأن الله تعالى: {ليس كمثله شيء وهو السميع البصير}
cards.why: 42:11 ends 'the Hearing, the Seeing': affirmation right after the denial of likeness.

cards.title: They do not deny what He affirmed
cards.ar: فلا ينفون عنه: ما وصف به نفسه.
cards.en: So they do not strip from Him what He said of Himself, nor 'twist words from their places', the Qur'an's phrase (4:46, 5:13).

cards.title: No ilhad in His names, no likening of His attributes
cards.ar: ولا يلحدون في: أسماء الله، وآياته.
cards.en: They do not deviate (ilhad) in Allah's names and signs, and they do not liken His attributes to the attributes of His creation.

cards.ask: Which does the book say Ahl al-Sunna do NOT do?

options.text: Deny what He said of Himself
Deviate in His names and signs
Affirm what the Messenger said of Him

source: فلا ينفون عنه: ما وصف به نفسه.
ولا يلحدون في: أسماء الله، وآياته.
cards.why: Four denials: no stripping, no twisting, no ilhad, no likening. Affirming and believing are what they do.

cards.title: No namesake, no equal, no rival
cards.ar: لأنه سبحانه؛ لا سمي له، ولا كفو له، ولا ند له،
cards.en: The reason: He has no namesake (samiyy), no equal (kufu') and no rival (nidd), and He is not measured against His creation.

cards.title: He knows Himself best
cards.ar: فإنه سبحانه؛ أعلم بنفسه وبغيره، وأصدق قيلا، وأحسن حديثا من خلقه.
cards.en: He knows Himself and others best, is the most truthful in speech and the best in discourse of all His creation: so what He says of Himself is taken over what anyone else says.

cards.ask: Why is what Allah says of Himself preferred to what people reason out?
options: He knows Himself best and speaks most truly
Because reason cannot speak of Allah at all
Because the scholars agreed by vote
cards.source: فإنه سبحانه؛ أعلم بنفسه وبغيره، وأصدق قيلا، وأحسن حديثا من خلقه.
cards.why: a'lamu bi-nafsihi, asdaqu qilan: most knowing of Himself, most truthful in word.

cards.title: Then His messengers
cards.ar: ثم رسله صادقون مصدقون؛ بخلاف الذين يقولون عليه ما لا يعلمون.
cards.en: Then His messengers are truthful and believed, unlike those who say of Him what they do not know.

cards.title: The verse that sums it up
cards.ar: فسبح نفسه عما وصفه به المخالفون للرسل، وسلم على المرسلين لسلامة ما قالوه من النقص والعيب.
cards.en: 37:180–182: Allah declared Himself above what the opponents of the messengers describe, and sent peace on the messengers because what they said is free of defect and fault.

cards.ar: وهو سبحانه قد جمع فيما وصف وسمى به نفسه بين: ____
cards.source: وهو سبحانه قد جمع فيما وصف وسمى به نفسه بين: النفي والإثبات.
cards.why: al-nafy wa-l-ithbat: denying what does not befit Him, affirming what He affirmed.

cards.title: Denial and affirmation together
cards.ar: وهو سبحانه قد جمع فيما وصف وسمى به نفسه بين: النفي والإثبات.
cards.en: In how He described and named Himself He joined denial (nafy: nothing is like Him) and affirmation (ithbat: He is the Hearing, the Seeing). Ahl al-Sunna keep both.

cards.title: No turning from what the messengers brought
cards.ar: فلا عدول لأهل السنة والجماعة عما جاءت به المرسلون.
cards.en: So Ahl al-Sunna do not turn away from what the messengers brought: it is the straight path, the path of those Allah favoured, the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous (4:69).

parts.title: The verses that describe Him
kitabs: آية الكرسي أعظم آية في كتاب الله

cards.title: A third of the Qur'an
cards.ar: ما وصف به نفسه في «سورة الإخلاص» التي تعدل ثلث القرآن.
cards.en: First among what Allah said of Himself: Surat al-Ikhlas, which equals a third of the Qur'an (sahih hadith): the commentators explain that the Qur'an is rulings, reports and tawhid, and this sura is pure tawhid. It equals a third in reward; it does not replace reciting the whole.

cards.ask: Fill the gap from Surat al-Ikhlas as the book quotes it.
cards.ar: حيث يقول: {قل هو الله أحد • الله الصمد • ____ • ولم يكن له كفوا أحد}
cards.source: حيث يقول: {قل هو الله أحد • الله الصمد • لم يلد ولم يولد • ولم يكن له كفوا أحد}
cards.why: 112:3: He neither begets nor is begotten.

cards.title: The greatest verse
cards.ar: وما وصف به نفسه في أعظم آية في كتابه.
cards.en: Then Ayat al-Kursi (2:255), the greatest verse in His Book: the Living, the Sustaining, whom neither drowsiness nor sleep takes, whose Kursi encompasses the heavens and the earth.

cards.ask: Which attributes does Ayat al-Kursi name, as quoted here?

options.text: Neither drowsiness nor sleep takes Him

cards.source: حيث يقول: {الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم لا تأخذه سنة ولا نوم
cards.why: Life, sustaining all, and no drowsiness or sleep: the verse's opening, as quoted here.

cards.title: Its protection
cards.ar: ولهذا كان من قرأ هذه الآية في ليلة؛ لم يزل عليه من الله حافظ، ولا يقربه شيطان حتى يصبح.
cards.en: For this reason whoever recites it at night has a guardian from Allah over him, and no devil comes near him until morning: the hadith of Abu Hurayra in al-Bukhari.

cards.ask: What does reciting Ayat al-Kursi at night bring, according to the book?
options: A guardian from Allah, and no devil near until morning
Forgiveness of every sin committed that day and the day before
The reward of reciting a third of the whole Qur'an that night
cards.source: لم يزل عليه من الله حافظ، ولا يقربه شيطان حتى يصبح.
cards.why: hafiz min Allah... la yaqrabuhu shaytan hatta yusbih.

lessons.title: Life, knowledge, power, hearing and sight

cards.title: Life
cards.ar: وقوله سبحانه: {وتوكل على الحي الذي لا يموت}
cards.en: Life (al-hayat): 'Rely on the Living who does not die' (25:58). The book's method from here on: each attribute is shown by the verses that state it, with little or no comment added.

cards.title: Knowledge
cards.ar: وقوله سبحانه: {هو الأول والآخر والظاهر والباطن وهو بكل شيء عليم}
cards.en: Knowledge (al-'ilm): He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward, and He knows all things (57:3); the keys of the unseen are with Him, no leaf falls but He knows it (6:59).

cards.ar: {وعنده مفاتح الغيب لا يعلمها إلا هو ويعلم ما في البر والبحر وما تسقط من ____ إلا يعلمها
cards.source: {وعنده مفاتح الغيب لا يعلمها إلا هو ويعلم ما في البر والبحر وما تسقط من ورقة إلا يعلمها
cards.why: 'no leaf falls but He knows it': knowledge down to a single leaf.

cards.title: Power
cards.ar: وقوله: {إن الله هو الرزاق ذو القوة المتين}
cards.en: Power (al-quwwa): 'Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm' (51:58).

cards.title: Hearing and sight
cards.ar: وقوله: {ليس كمثله شيء وهو السميع البصير}
cards.en: Hearing and sight (al-sam' wa-l-basar): 'There is nothing like Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing' (42:11), and 'Allah is ever Hearing, Seeing' (4:58).

cards.ask: Match each verse to the attribute the book files it under.
items: وتوكل على الحي الذي لا يموت
source: {هو الأول والآخر والظاهر والباطن وهو بكل شيء عليم}
{إن الله هو الرزاق ذو القوة المتين}
{إن الله نعما يعظكم به إن الله كان سميعا بصيرا}
cards.why: Each verse sits under the heading of the attribute it states.

cards.title: Will
cards.ar: وقوله: {ولو شاء الله ما اقتتل الذين من بعدهم من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات ولكن اختلفوا فمنهم من آمن ومنهم من كفر ولو شاء الله ما اقتتلوا ولكن الله يفعل ما يريد}
cards.en: Will (al-irāda): 'had Allah willed they would not have fought... but Allah does what He wills' (2:253). The commentators divide His will in two: kawniyya (cosmic, the same as mashīʾa: it always comes to pass, whether He loves the thing or not) and sharʿiyya (religious: what He loves and commands, which may or may not be done by His slaves).

cards.title: Guidance by His will
cards.ar: وقوله: {فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام ومن يرد أن يضله يجعل صدره ضيقا حرجا كأنما يصعد في السماء}
cards.en: 'Whomever Allah wills to guide, He opens his breast to Islam; whomever He wills to lead astray, He makes his breast tight and narrow' (6:125): guidance is in His will.

cards.ask: Whom does Allah love, in the verses the book quotes?
source: {فما استقاموا لكم فاستقيموا لهم إن الله يحب المتقين}

cards.title: Love
cards.ar: وقوله: {وأحسنوا إن الله يحب المحسنين}
cards.en: Love (al-mahabba): Allah loves those who do good (2:195), the just (49:9), the God-fearing (9:7), those who repent and purify themselves (2:222), and a people He loves who love Him (5:54). Note: the Ashʿarī school reads 'love' as His will to reward; this book affirms it as a real attribute befitting Him. Nothing is asked on that.

cards.ar: {قل إن كنتم تحبون الله ____ يحببكم الله ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم}
cards.source: {قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم}
cards.why: fa-ttabi'uni: following the Prophet is how Allah's love is won.

cards.title: Pleasure
cards.ar: وقوله: {رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه}
cards.en: Pleasure (al-rida): 'Allah is pleased with them and they with Him' (98:8).

cards.title: Mercy
cards.ar: وقوله: {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم}
cards.en: Mercy (al-rahma): the Basmala itself (27:30), 'our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge' (40:7), 'He is ever Merciful to the believers' (33:43), 'your Lord has prescribed mercy upon Himself' (6:54).

cards.ar: {كتب ربكم على نفسه ____}
cards.why: kataba 'ala nafsihi al-rahma: He prescribed mercy upon Himself.

cards.ask: Sort each attribute by the group the book's commentators give it.
cards.why: Life and knowledge He always has (dhātiyya). Love, pleasure and a particular mercy toward someone are tied in the texts to His will and to a cause (fiʿliyya). Mercy itself, the commentators add, is of the essence in its root and of act in each instance. Acts are eternal in their kind, each instance happening when He wills.
